The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for over 42.30 lakh farmers not covered under Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), a ₹5,548-crore provision for the Narmada-Tapi diversion project in Nandurbar, confiscation of assets of firms involved in financial fraud, and a law to regulate private-aided schools, among 14 decisions.

At the meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, the Cabinet decided to give free foodgrains to farmers who are not covered under the National Food Security Act in 33 drought-affected districts of the State. The beneficiaries belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.

“The farmers will receive five kg of foodgrains per person every month, free of cost, for the next three months. This will include three kg rice and two kg wheat,” stated a release issued from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).

With an aim to strengthen the irrigation system in Nandurbar district, the Cabinet gave nod to the Narmada-Tapi diversion project. This will include six diversions weirs that aim to benefit around 26,526 hectares with irrigation while generating 11.50 MW power, as per the Water Resources Department officials.

The Maharashtra government has also approved the plan to set up a separate MPID (Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors) tribunal with a time limit of 90 days for the disposal of cases. The Cabinet also decided to expedite the process of confiscating properties of institutions committing financial fraud and amend the MPID Act,” stated the CMO.

The State government has also decided to increase the hostel allowances for students from Economically Weaker Sections (EBC, SEBC and EWS) pursuing professional degree courses in health sciences under the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme. It also approved the provision of financial facilities for teachers through RBI-registered institutions.

The Cabinet approved the draft Maharashtra Private-Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, which will be tabled in the legislature. The move aims to provide a comprehensive law to be enacted for regulation of private-aided schools, the CMO statement added.

The Cabinet also cleared a draft bill to amend the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021, to exclude acupuncture as a system of treatment from its purview, the release said.

In another decision, librarians working in private-aided Ayurveda and Unani colleges will be granted revised pay scales in accordance with the recommendations of the Seventh Pay Commission, on a par with full-time librarians in government medical, dental and Ayurveda colleges.

2. articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

India’s satellite supply chain is “highly dependent” on imports for critical components and the private sector’s contribution is limited to “structural assemblies” and “propulsion components” largely supplied by established public sector firms and vintage private firms, said a report by IN-SPACe, India’s regulatory-cum-promotional body for the private space sector.
While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead.

Science Minister Jitendra Singh earlier this week said that India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to increase to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector set to grow from a a few startups “to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years”.

The Supply Chain Landscape of Satellite Manufacturing in India report, which was made public on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), says that nearly 60% of satellite costs were attributed to electronic, electrical and electromechanical components, and specialised materials, many of which are imported.
India also has limited testing and certification facilities, which weakened prospects for acceptance in global markets.
Many companies largely operated on a “project-based manufacturing model”, which disincentivised long-term investment in automation and production capacity, the report noted.
Critical components often took a long time to procure – frequently 12-16 months – which led to project delays and hobbled responsiveness to market opportunities.

There was also a shortage of trained and skilled personnel in satellite systems engineering, quality assurance, testing and qualification, besides limited private-sector research and development and technology transfer.
The report was prepared by Brijesh Kumar Sol and Yudhishthir J. of IN-SPACe and “approved” by Pawan Goenka, IN-SPACe chairman.
The report isn’t a statistical survey, but paints a descriptive map of India’s satellite manufacturing supply chain.

articles.title: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists

The Election Commission of India on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) directed that any incorrect or erroneous entries flagged in the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR) would be corrected using Form 8 after comparing the entries with the corresponding information collected during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
All the changes would be made after verification by the concerned officials and not through automated matching.
Form 8 is the ECI application for correction in voter details.
The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists.
The directive was given to the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and UTs where the SIR has been completed and SSR is on.

The States and UTs are Andaman and Nicobar Island, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Karnataka and Meghalaya.
The ECI had ordered the SSR of electoral rolls with reference to January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date in these States/UTs through letters on October 15, November 4 and November 11.

In its directive on Wednesday, the poll body said: “In order to identify and rectify any probable incorrect or erroneous entries in the particulars of electors (such as name, relation name or type, date of birth, mobile number, photograph, etc.) in the existing electoral rolls during the ongoing SSR, the existing electoral particulars of the concerned electors shall be compared with the corresponding information collected during the SIR.”
“Wherever any mismatch is noticed, the same shall be flagged for verification and for taking necessary corrective action,” it said.
In respect of such flagged entries, the BLOs shall visit the concerned electors during the ongoing SSR to verify their particulars and obtain a duly filled-in and signed Form 8, wherever is required.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court quashes postal ballot tampering case against former Chikkamagaluru DC, BJP leader Jeevaraj
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court of Karnataka has quashed criminal case registered in 2026 against former Chikkamagaluru Deputy Commissioner K.N. Ramesh, Returning Officer Vedamurthy T.R. and BJP leader D.N. Jeevaraj over alleged tampering of postal ballots after counting of votes in 2023 in the elections held to Sringeri Assembly constituency

The High Court of Karnataka has quashed criminal case registered in 2026 against former Chikkamagaluru Deputy Commissioner K.N. Ramesh, Returning Officer Vedamurthy T.R. and BJP leader D.N. Jeevaraja over alleged tampering of postal ballots after counting of votes in 2023 in the elections held to Sringeri Assembly constituency.

Quashing the First Information Report registered in May 2026, Justice M. Nagaprasanna ruled that the inordinate and unexplained three-year delay in registering the complaint vitiated the criminal prosecution.

The court noted that ballot boxes were sealed and locked in strong rooms under strict police security since May 13, 2023, and were opened in May 2026 following the court’s April 2026 order on Mr. Jeevaraj’s election petition challenging the legality of election of Congress candidate T.D. Raje Gowda.

The court, while partly allowing election petition on April 6, 2026, had ordered re-verification of 279 postal ballots that were rejected during counting of votes in 2023 and recount of all postal ballots if any rejected postal ballots were found to be in order during re-verification. Mr. Jeevaraj was declared elected after completion of recounting of the postal ballots on May 3, 2026. However, operation of result of recounting was subsequently stayed by the Supreme Court.

Hours after declaration of result of recounting, one Sudhir Kumar Murolli, a counting booth agent for Mr. Raje Gowda, filed the complaint alleging that a crucial document, known as “ballot paper account” sheets, was tampered with back in 2023 itself after obtaining signature of agents of all the candidates.

“If there was doubt about the counting earlier in the year 2023, nothing stopped the complainant from registering the complaint immediately thereafter. With the declaration of the results after recounting in which the candidate loses and Mr. Jeevaraj is declared as a winning candidate, investigation by the jurisdictional police on a complaint cannot emerge. It is undoubtedly hit by delay. Due to delay, there has been lot of embellishments in the complaint,” the High Court said.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The band’s imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as ‘Girls on Film’ and ‘Union of the Snake’ and the moody ballads ‘The Chauffeur’ and ‘Save a Prayer’

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran , whose huge pop hits include “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life, he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed,” the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Music Award recipients.

The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as “Girls on Film” and “Union of the Snake” and the moody ballads “The Chauffeur” and “Save a Prayer”. Other hits in the coming years included “The Wild Boys,” “New Moon on Monday” and “Come Undone.” Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song “A View to a Kill” and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesisers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan, and that meant a lot to the band.

articles.title: IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up.

It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities.

Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence.

Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: Court rejects PG operator’s bail in Satya Niketan building collapse case, says he put profits above students’ lives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,’ the court said

Observing that he appeared to have placed financial gains above the safety of students and labourers staying at the premises, a Delhi court on Monday refused to grant bail to Shubham Tyagi, one of operator of the paying guest (PG) accommodation in South Delhi’s Satya Niketan which collapsed in September this year leaving seven dead.

Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana of Patiala House Court denied bail to the accuse after rejecting Mr Tyagi’s argument that he had no responsibility for the construction of the PG which he has co-accused Sudhanshu Kumar had rented the property from its owners and operated a boy’s hostel.

It added that even if the construction was not being carried out under Mr Tyagi’s instructions, he was obligated to ensure that residents vacated the building until the work was completed. He was also expected to alert occupants about the potential structural danger.

“The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,” court said.

Holding that Mr Tyagi could have anticipated the risks arising from alleged unauthorised construction and structural alterations court mentioned the statement of injured student Nitish Chhib, court said that it was alleged that basement construction had continued for 10-12 days despite complaints from students. The residents were allegedly threatened with eviction when they objected to the work.

Emphasising the gravity of the incident, the court observed that building collapses linked to illegal construction have repeatedly resulted in fatalities and must be treated seriously. It remarked that those allegedly responsible for the loss of seven lives did not deserve discretionary relief and that such incidents required a firm judicial response.
Denying bail, court also stated that the trial is at an early stage and public witnesses were yet to be examined and there was a possibility of witness intimidation.

The Delhi Police had filed a 638-page chargesheet in the matter earlier this month. It named building owner Hariram Gupta, his wife Urmila Gupta, their son Mahesh Gupta, labour contractor Sanoj Kumar and PG operators Mr Tyagi and Mr Kumar as accused.

articles.title: Maharashtra FDA cancels Inducare’s manufacturing licences again over nine unauthorised drugs, two found spurious
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Firm manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission; drugs worth ₹1.72 crore seized from YCM Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts.

The cancellation order, issued on November 23 by the Joint Commissioner (Drugs), Pune Division, directed the firm to immediately cease all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

Of the nine drugs tested, two were declared spurious after government analysts found that the claimed active ingredients were absent. Ibucare Plus, a combination of ibuprofen and paracetamol, contained no ibuprofen, while Carevita-M, a multivitamin tablet, was found to contain none of the nine specified ingredients tested.

The remaining drugs failed various quality tests, with several containing significantly lower quantities of active ingredients than claimed on their labels. These included medicines used in the treatment of cardiovascular and digestive disorders.
The FDA said the firm, located in the Additional MIDC area of Jejuri in Pune district, had admitted in its written response that it had not obtained separate product permissions for the nine drugs.

The firm’s manufacturing licences had previously been cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection conducted on July 14 and 15 revealed 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).

The inspection revealed that approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of Caregyl-400 had been manufactured without mandatory batch manufacturing and packing records or test reports. Of these, 5.20 lakh tablets had already been distributed. Laboratory analysis revealed that the sampled batch contained only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole content.

Several samples of substandard drugs were also collected from the Central Medical Store of Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial (YCM) Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad, following which stocks worth approximately ₹1.72 crore were seized on November 4.
Other irregularities included discrepancies in manufacturing and expiry dates, inadequate laboratory testing procedures, unhygienic manufacturing conditions and improper storage of finished products.
A show-cause notice was issued to the firm on October 29, following which it submitted a written response on November 3. A personal hearing was conducted on November 23.

articles.title: Mumbai Police announce traffic curbs for VBA’s Samvidhan Samman Mahasabha at Shivaji Park
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The annual public rally, held ahead of Constitution Day on November 26, is being organised under the leadership of VBA national president Prakash Ambedkar

The Mumbai Traffic Police on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announced traffic restrictions in Dadar and adjoining areas from 9 a.m. to 11.50 p.m. on Wednesday (November 25) in view of the Samvidhan Samman Mahasabha organised by the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) at Shivaji Park.
The annual public rally, held ahead of Constitution Day on November 26, is being organised under the leadership of VBA national president Prakash Ambedkar.
With a large number of people expected to arrive from across Maharashtra, the police anticipate traffic congestion on the Western and Eastern Express Highways and roads leading to the venue.

According to the notification issued by Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Dipali Dhate, vehicular entry will be prohibited on Swatantryaveer Savarkar Marg between Siddhivinayak Temple junction and Kapad Bazar junction in Mahim. Motorists will be diverted through S.K. Bole Road, Agar Bazar, Portuguese Church and Gokhale Road.

Vehicular entry will also be prohibited between Raja Badhe Chowk and Keluskar Marg (North), on the southbound stretch of Lt. Dilip Gupte Marg from Pandurang Naik Marg junction, and between Gadkari Chowk and Keluskar Road (South).
Depending on traffic conditions, the police may also close stretches of Bal Govindas Marg and Dadasaheb Rege Marg.

Parking restrictions will be imposed on eight roads or road stretches, including Swatantryaveer Savarkar Marg, Keluskar Road (North and South), M.B. Raut Road, Pandurang Naik Marg, Dadasaheb Rege Marg, Lt. Dilip Gupte Marg, N.C. Kelkar Marg and L.J. Road.
Parking facilities have been designated at Kohinoor Square and Senapati Bapat Road in Dadar, Five Gardens in Matunga and R.A.K. Road in Wadala.

articles.title: Contract awarded to ITI Ltd. for printing licences, RCs followed due tender procedures, Kerala High Court told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State government has informed the Kerala High Court that the contract awarded to ITI Limited, Bengaluru, for printing driving licences and registration certificates (RCs) during the tenure of Director General of Police S. Sreejith as Transport Commissioner had followed due tender procedures.

Justice A. Badharudeen had sought details of the tender awarded on a plea filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Malappuram, raising allegations of corruption and fund misappropriation against Mr. Sreejith.

Mr. Edavana had claimed that Mr. Sreejith awarded the printing contract after confirming an agreement with another company in March 2023. In this regard, the court had directed the State to clarify whether the contract procedures were completed properly and to specify the amounts disbursed both before and after April 2023.

K.R. Jyothilal, Additional Chief Secretary (Home), said that the contract was signed at the rate of ₹60 per card plus GST for printing non-chip PVC cards. The five-year contract was signed on April 15, 2023. He also explained that the company was paid more than ₹37.70 crore for printing licences and RCs to date.

Mr. Jyothilal explained that there had been an extensive legal dispute regarding the tender, which was ultimately placed before the Supreme Court. He also produced the Government Order ratifying all actions taken by then Transport Commissioner, Mr. Sreejith, as part of entering into an agreement with ITI Limited.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

articles.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, U.S. jury finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds

A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.
However, jurors acquitted the company of the most serious charge it faced: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy to steal intellectual property from American companies.
The verdict followed a lengthy trial in which U.S. prosecutors argued that Huawei repeatedly stole technological secrets from competitors and partners in the U.S. and elsewhere.

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

Lawyers for the company said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of Huawei's more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn't actually exist.

It's unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei's global fortunes. The company hasn't been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

That hasn't stopped the company from doing a robust business elsewhere. Its smartphones and other telecom equipment are sold globally. More recently, it has expanded into chipmaking as the boom in artificial intelligence fuels demand for microprocessors, becoming an important alternative in China to chips made by companies such as Nvidia.
The U.S. announced its criminal charges against Huawei in early 2019 and later expanded the allegations.
Chinese officials said the U.S. has engaged in “economic bullying” and improperly used national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies.

The indictment against Huawei accused it of a long pattern of outright technology theft. Huawei, prosecutors said, once sold internet routers containing source code copied from a competitor. In another episode, a person working for Huawei slipped into a competitor's booth at a Chicago trade show to surreptitiously photograph the circuits inside another company's networking device, the indictment said. Prosecutors said that on another occasion, a Huawei worker removed a robotic arm from a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured.

Both must meet prescribed chemical and microbiological safety standards.

articles.title: Behind Ramdev-Dhirendra Shastri exchange, a jockeying for relevance in poll-bound U.P.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Even before the political backlash over his comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna could die down, Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri faced thinly veiled criticism from yoga guru Baba Ramdev

Two ‘babas’, both perceived as close to the BJP, are facing off as religious and political activities gain pace in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh. Even before the political backlash over his comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna could die down, Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Krishna Shastri faced thinly veiled criticism from yoga guru Baba Ramdev, who on Monday (November 23, 2026) called those who draw such analogies “hypocrites”.

Mr. Shastri shied away from escalating the exchange, but the spat has drawn attention as the political plot thickens in India’s most populous State. Political observers see the exchange against the backdrop of caste equations in Uttar Pradesh and Mr. Ramdev’s bid to remain in relevance as a 30-year-old gains increasing traction with his religious discourses in the Hindi heartland.

Although Mr. Shastri subsequently apologised for hurting devotees’ sentiments, the controversy got second wind on Monday when Mr. Ramdev offered his take during a religious event in Jamshedpur. “Those who made comparisons between gods and goddesses – ‘Ram is great, Krishna is crooked’ – and later apologised are hypocrites... Nobody in society has the right to say such petty things. There is decorum, discipline and protocol for everything,” he said without naming anyone.

Mr. Shastri chose to pipe down in response, describing Mr. Ramdev as his “senior and guardian”. On cue, the yoga guru, in Haridwar on Tuesday, softened his position, calling Mr. Shastri his “younger brother” and saying his criticism “came out of affection”.

The two have shared platforms in the past, including at BJP national media in-charge Anil Baluni’s Deepavali-linked celebration in Delhi on November 20. Days earlier, Mr. Ramdev also attended a Ram Katha (discourse) in Kunda, U.P., headlined by Mr. Shastri that was organised by Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, a seven-term MLA and founder of the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik). It was attended by several prominent political figures, including Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, Minister Suresh Khanna, former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, former Union Minister Sanjeev Balyan and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey.

While Mr. Shastri emerges as a prominent face of a younger generation of Hindu preachers, attracting large crowds to his religious congregations and building a substantial social media following, Mr. Ramdev has seen his once prominent public profile face challenges. One of the key supporters during the BJP’s rise to power in 2014, he built a national identity around yoga, nationalism and Patanjali Ayurved. In recent years, however, he has faced backlash over Supreme Court proceedings pertaining to his company’s misleading advertisements.

As a preacher-on-the-rise and a veteran yoga guru jostle for influence, the BJP’s efforts to marshal a spectrum of castes and communities to prevail in a high-voltage election means cultivating both – the first a Brahmin and other a Yadav.

“Many of those who have made such statements in the past have faced legal action and even arrests. As nothing of this sort has happened here, it shows that the Baba (Mr. Shastri) may have ruling party’s support. But how the BJP is going to handle this matter where two of its own poster boys are fighting will be interesting to watch,” said Shashi Kant Pandey, who teaches political science at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Central University in Lucknow.

articles.title: Arrangements in place for Mission Chakkakompan; Kerala Forest dept to tranquilize wild tusker
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Forest department also plans to dart Murivali in Chinnakkanal

As the Forest Department and district administration completed arrangements on Tuesday to tranquilize and fit a radio collar to Chakkakompan at Chinnakkanal in the Devikulam forest range on Wednesday, officials said they are also planning to fit a radio collar to Murivali, another “problematic” wild elephant in the area.
District Collector has issued prohibitory orders in several wards of the Chinnakkanal panchayat ahead of the operation, officials said.
According to Chief Conservator of Forests D.K. Vinod Kumar, the mission is expected to take place on Wednesday once the elephant approaches Vilakku in Chinnakkanal.

“Officials have been directed to identify additional spots in the area to conduct the operation,” Mr. Kumar said. “After the mission, the team will remain in Chinnakkanal for two more days as it plans to attach a radio collar to Murivali, another problematic female elephant. A proposal to dart Murivali will be submitted to the Chief Wildlife Warden . The animal is currently in Mathikettan Shola and needs to move toward Chinnakkanal before we can conduct the operation.”
Two high-quality radio collars were sourced from abroad, he said.
Mr. Kumar noted that a study by a Professor at the Wildlife Institute of India found that wild elephants’ aggressive behaviour decreases after they are fitted with radio collars.
Elephants are now getting aggressive, increasing human–elephant conflicts. Wild elephants in Chinnakkanal have reached an aggressive level, said Mr. Kumar.

He added that installing the radio collar is the first step, and if the animal continues to pose a threat, the Forest department will take further action to translocate it from the Chinnakkanal region.

Two kumkis (trained elephants) named Vikram and Bharat have arrived in Chinnakkanal to assist with the operation, officials said. On Tuesday, the Forest department conducted a mock drill at Cement Palam, near Chinnakkanal, ahead of Mission Chakkakompan. Munnar Divisional Forest Officer Saju Varghese led the drill, which included an expert team, veterinary doctors and Rapid Response Team members.

As part of Mission Chakkakompan, the District Collector declared a holiday on Wednesday for schools, tuition centers and anganwadis in wards 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 and 12 of the Chinnakkanal panchayat. The Collector also banned night camps and campfires in those wards on Wednesday.

articles.title: Kerala HC declines to interfere with State govt’s reconstitution of Waqf Board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Court says State Waqf Board was already functional
The Kerala High Court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) declined to interfere with the Keralam government’s decision to reconstitute the State Waqf Board, saying that it was already functional.

A Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was hearing appeals by K S Hamza and C K Usman Haji, the former chairperson and member of the earlier board that was disbanded barely eight months into its five-year term, against a single judge order declining to stay the reconstitution of the board.
The single judge, on October 17, had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board but said that it would be subject to the outcome of the petitions challenging the same.

The judge had also tagged the petitions by Hamza and Haji with the earlier PILs – challenging the validity of the previous and now disbanded board – which were pending before a Bench headed by Chief Justice Soumen Sen.
However, the Bench headed by the Chief Justice on October 19 dismissed the PILs as the board had been reconstituted.
On Tuesday, the Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji directed the Registry that the earlier petitions of Hamza and Haji be listed before the appropriate Bench.

Court says State Waqf Board was already functional

The Kerala High Court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) declined to interfere with the Keralam government’s decision to reconstitute the State Waqf Board, saying that it was already functional.

A Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji was hearing appeals by K S Hamza and C K Usman Haji, the former chairperson and member of the earlier board that was disbanded barely eight months into its five-year term, against a single judge order declining to stay the reconstitution of the board.

The single judge, on October 17, had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board but said that it would be subject to the outcome of the petitions challenging the same.

The judge had also tagged the petitions by Hamza and Haji with the earlier PILs – challenging the validity of the previous and now disbanded board – which were pending before a Bench headed by Chief Justice Soumen Sen.

However, the Bench headed by the Chief Justice on October 19 dismissed the PILs as the board had been reconstituted.

On Tuesday, the Bench of justices Devan Ramachandran and Basant Balaji directed the Registry that the earlier petitions of Hamza and Haji be listed before the appropriate Bench.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: After the 9/11 attacks, Mr. Giuliani ‌became one of the most popular figures in U.S. politics. He launched a Republican presidential ‌bid ⁠in 2007, and even after it failed, he remained a prominent conservative ⁠messenger

President Donald Trump ‌on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) awarded the Medal of Freedom, the country’s highest civilian honor, to ​Rudy Giuliani, the former New York Mayor who became a national figure after ⁠the September 11, 2001, attacks and later helped Trump try to overturn his 2020 election defeat.

Mr. Trump announced he would honour Mr. Giuliani, 82, in September 2025 shortly after the former Mayor was badly injured in a ‌car accident. Mr. Trump at the time called him “the greatest Mayor in the history of New York City, and an equally great American Patriot.”

After the 9/11 attacks, Mr. Giuliani ‌became one of the most popular figures in U.S. politics. He launched a Republican presidential ‌bid ⁠in 2007, and even after it failed, he remained a prominent conservative ⁠messenger.
In a statement, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales called Mr. Giuliani “a dedicated public servant whose decisive leadership has left a lasting impact on New York City and our nation.”
Mr. Trump awarded the medal in a private Oval Office ceremony.

Mr. Giuliani ​in a statement said he was “honored ‌and humbled” by the medal, and credited advice from President Ronald Reagan, under whom he served as Associate Attorney General and a U.S. Attorney, for guiding his public service.
“I share the credit with all the men and women who worked with me, disagreed with me, ‌and loved me — particularly those who lost their lives in the causes we ​undertook together,” Mr. Giuliani said.

His son, former Trump administration official Andrew Giuliani, told reporters outside the White House that the ceremony was a “special” gathering in which Mr. Trump ⁠and Mr. Giuliani reminisced about their long friendship.

Their alliance deepened after Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election. Mr. Giuliani advanced falsehoods about the result and the integrity of the voting process. He held a press conference ‌at a Philadelphia landscaping business, where he made claims that were widely rebutted, then another at the headquarters of the Republican National Committee where hair dye dribbled down his face.

His false claims came with legal consequences. He was barred from practising law in New York, where he once served as the U.S. Attorney in the state’s southern district, and Washington, and faced criminal charges in Georgia and Arizona for attempting to subvert the 2020 election results.

articles.title: Three Fort Hood shooting survivors lose final appeal to witness Nidal Hasan’s execution
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasan was found guilty of multiple counts of murder and attempted murder related to those killed and the more than 30 who were wounded by gunfire in the attack

Three survivors of the shooting at Fort Hood will not be allowed to witness the execution of Nidal Hasan, who fatally shot 13 people in the attack at the Texas Army post in 2009, military officials said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
Hasan was found guilty of multiple counts of murder and attempted murder related to those killed and the more than 30 who were wounded by gunfire in the attack.

On November 10, the Army said the three cannot attend the execution scheduled for December 3 because none of them was the direct victim of those charges, citing regulations governing military executions. An email sent on Tuesday (November 24) and shared with The Associated Press by recipients said military officials rejected their request for reconsideration, citing security and space issues.

The three argued that the Army should apply a broader definition of “victim” from the Uniform Code of Military Justice that says a victim can be someone who suffered “direct physical, emotional or pecuniary harm.” They argued that the military's refusal to allow them to attend was saying they had not been victims because they were not struck by bullets.
A previous plan to livestream the military execution, the first since 1961 and the first by firing squad since World War II, was rescinded after bipartisan backlash.
The letter signed by the commandant of Fort Leavenworth, the military prison where Hasan is being held, said the three cannot appeal again.
“Please understand that this is not meant as a judgment on any emotional injury you or others suffered as a result of CP Hasan's crimes,” it said.
Retired Colonel Kathy Platoni, who would have been Hasan's supervisor during a planned deployment to Afghanistan, said the denial felt like a betrayal.
“I would desperately like to attend,” Ms. Platoni said from her home in Ohio. “To look Hasan in the eye and say, You didn't get me.'”
The Army noted in a statement that regulations specify who can witness a military execution, and reiterated the size and space restrictions.

articles.title: Huawei says U.S. conviction 'without legal or factual merit'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The world's leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei has been targeted by U.S. President Donald Trump's administration

A U.S. jury convicted Huawei on Tuesday of stealing trade secrets and lying to regulators over its work with Iran, according to the Department of Justice, with the Chinese tech giant Huawei threatening to hit back with legal action.
The world's leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei has been targeted by U.S. President Donald Trump's administration , which alleges a risk of it spying on behalf of the Chinese government.
The United States has previously urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for the rollout of new 5G mobile networks.

The verdict followed a three-month trial at a New York federal court, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) reported, with jurors finding Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it, including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States.

"No person or company is above the law," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. "For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft."

The jury did, however, acquit the company of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice, a move Huawei said in a statement it "welcomed," adding that it "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years."

"We believe the government's remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit... We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests," the statement continued.
The charges in part involved Huawei's business dealings with the government of Iran.

"Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran's government, military, or intelligence community," DOJ said.

"Huawei lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of US dollars and access to US-dollar clearing services, which enabled Huawei to be a sophisticated participant in a global marketplace for telecommunications services - in part because of its lies."

articles.title: Bangladesh garment workers win 36% wage rise
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The South Asian nation, the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread protests since October by workers demanding higher pay
Bangladesh’s garment workers won a 36% minimum wage increase on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after lengthy negotiations with factory owners, officials said.
The South Asian nation, the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread protests since October by workers demanding higher pay.
After the deal was struck, workers’ representatives urged people to return to factories.
“Although we are not completely satisfied, the outcome is not entirely bad either,” Babul Akhter, the workers’ representative, told reporters.
“Previously, workers used to get a wage revision every five years, but this time they are getting a revised wage after three years.”
Workers initially demanded a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($240), up from the current 12,500 taka.
Workers say their pay has failed to keep pace with the rising cost of food, housing, transport and health care.

Judge Syed Azad Subhani, the chairman of the country’s government-appointed garment industry wage board, said the “majority supported a minimum wage of 17,000 taka” ($139), after a vote early Wednesday.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association said on Sunday that protests had cost the industry an estimated $428 million in losses, while orders worth $254 million had shifted to other countries.
The disruption came ahead of the busy Christmas season.

The South Asian nation, the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread protests since October by workers demanding higher pay

Bangladesh’s garment workers won a 36% minimum wage increase on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after lengthy negotiations with factory owners, officials said.

The South Asian nation, the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread protests since October by workers demanding higher pay.

After the deal was struck, workers’ representatives urged people to return to factories.

“Although we are not completely satisfied, the outcome is not entirely bad either,” Babul Akhter, the workers’ representative, told reporters.

“Previously, workers used to get a wage revision every five years, but this time they are getting a revised wage after three years.”

Workers initially demanded a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($240), up from the current 12,500 taka.

Workers say their pay has failed to keep pace with the rising cost of food, housing, transport and health care.

Judge Syed Azad Subhani, the chairman of the country’s government-appointed garment industry wage board, said the “majority supported a minimum wage of 17,000 taka” ($139), after a vote early Wednesday.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association said on Sunday that protests had cost the industry an estimated $428 million in losses, while orders worth $254 million had shifted to other countries.

The disruption came ahead of the busy Christmas season.

articles.title: Solomon Islands names Australia as its primary security partner in a new treaty that excludes China
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The new treaty confirms Australia's place as the Solomons' ‘primary security partner’ and states ‘there will be no foreign military or security base’ on the smaller nation 2,000 kilometres northeast of Australia

The Prime Ministers of Australia and the Solomon Islands signed a bilateral security pact on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) following reports that the tiny South Pacific island nation will end its secretive 4-year-old defense deal with China.

The new treaty confirms Australia's place as the Solomons' “primary security partner” and states “there will be no foreign military or security base” on the smaller nation 2,000 kilometres (1,200 miles) northeast of Australia, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale said in a statement.

The deal is the latest bilateral security pact Australia has struck with Pacific neighbors since Beijing inked a treaty with the Solomons' previous government in 2022 that created fears the Chinese navy would build a base in the South Pacific.

Mr. Wale would not confirm or deny news media reports that his government had told Beijing that the security pact with China, which has provided Chinese police trainers to the Solomons' capital, Honiara, would not be renewed when it expires after five years in early 2027.

“Unfortunately, there is a non-disclosure clause in the treaty with China,” Mr. Wale told reporters in a press conference with Albanese at Australian Parliament House. “So I am unable to talk about that. We have ongoing discussions with China.”
“As you know, Solomon Islands has been, for a number of years, a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done. Gone. We don't want to be there again,” he added.
In Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun did not directly answer a journalist's question about whether the Solomons had said it would end the Chinese security pact.
“China always follows the principle of mutual respect and equality in developing relations with the Solomon Islands,” Mr. Guo said on Tuesday (November 24).
“There is no element of geopolitical rivalry or bloc confrontation in cooperation between China and Pacific island countries, including the Solomon Islands,” he added.
Mr. Albanese said the new bilateral treaty elevated bilateral relations to a “level which has never been seen before and has never been stronger.”

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return brings open-weight AI debate to forefront in Washington
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s board announced on ​Monday that it would reinstate Mr. Huang as CEO, following his resignation over reports of extramarital affairs

Nvidia’s ​leadership crisis has thrust a tech industry squabble over open-weight AI models into the spotlight, where CEO Jensen Huang has become one of Washington’s ‌loudest voices for U.S. development of a technology now dominated by Chinese companies.

Nvidia’s board announced on ​Monday that it would reinstate Mr. Huang as CEO, following his resignation over reports of extramarital affairs , including with ⁠a woman who news reports said was suspected of spying for the Chinese government.

Before the scandal erupted, Mr. Huang had pushed the U.S. Congress and the Trump administration to support American companies developing open-weight AI models, which would align with his company’s commercial interests, although a debate has ‌raged over the models’ implications for U.S. national security.

U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration supports open-weight AI systems because they give startups dependable and cheaper options outside proprietary AI tools from providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
“The Trump ‌Administration’s clear and long-standing policy has been strong support for” open-weight AI models, a White House official said in ‌a ⁠statement to Reuters on Tuesday.

Mr. Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in the Nvidia board’s decision ⁠to reinstate Mr. Huang in part because they viewed him as the protector of U.S.-made open-weight AI models, people familiar with the matter said on Monday. The White House did not comment on the connection between the support for Mr. Huang and open-weight models.

Open-weight AI models, unlike closed models, make core components publicly ​available for users to download, modify and adapt for specific ‌tasks. Such models broaden demand for Nvidia’s chips and computing infrastructure beyond a handful of leading AI model developers, providing a business opportunity for Mr. Huang’s company.

Executives from closed-model developers such as Anthropic and OpenAI have expressed skepticism of open-weight models, according to their public statements, creating a schism in the AI sector. Anthropic and OpenAI earn revenue by selling ‌access to proprietary systems whose underlying technology they control.

“Any kind of political headwinds against Huang and Nvidia could be ​a harbinger for a crackdown on open weights, which is not good for little tech and companies that are trying to have a fighting chance of disrupting some of the incumbents,” said Luther Lowe ⁠of Y Combinator, a Silicon Valley incubator and startup fund.

In a letter earlier this year, Mr. Huang urged the U.S government to avoid “premature restrictions” on open-weight tools. A coalition of companies co-signed the letter, including venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, Microsoft and Palantir. Anthropic declined ‌to sign on.

articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after historic outage, internal memos show
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The November 12-13 outage ​hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms ⁠and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure

Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” drive to ​overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering ‌systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters.

The November 12-13 outage ​hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms ⁠and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.
Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. CEO ‌Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption.

The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft’s engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted ‌Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and ‌other ⁠Microsoft 365 products.
It was the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, ⁠M365 Core President Jason Henderson said in a memo to staff on Friday.
Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added.

Microsoft says services fully restored after hourslong global outage

Amanda ​Silver, Microsoft’s corporate vice president overseeing M365 ‌Core and Work IQ, the company’s workplace intelligence platform for AI agents, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers had to work through a “fog of war” as the outage unfolded.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he is in therapy as comeback rally fades
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board

Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.

"I made some terrible mistakes," Mr. Huang told an hourlong all-hands meeting at the company's Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a livestream of the event.
He told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board.
But Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday (November 23, 2026) that he had been in contact with directors about Mr. Huang's return. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he said. "And I convinced them."
After vaulting more than 30% on Monday (November 23, 2026), Nvidia shares were down about six percent at close on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."
So far Monday's surge was a "one day wonder...We are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.

Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.
Mr. Trump was reportedly talked into backing the return of the Taiwan-born CEO after top tech investors told him the U.S. economy and Wall Street depended on it.
Nvidia said Monday (November 23, 2026) that it had reinstated Mr. Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.

Jensen Huang told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board

Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.

"I made some terrible mistakes," Mr. Huang told an hourlong all-hands meeting at the company's Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a livestream of the event.

He told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board.

But Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday (November 23, 2026) that he had been in contact with directors about Mr. Huang's return. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he said. "And I convinced them."

After vaulting more than 30% on Monday (November 23, 2026), Nvidia shares were down about six percent at close on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."

So far Monday's surge was a "one day wonder...We are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.

Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.

Mr. Trump was reportedly talked into backing the return of the Taiwan-born CEO after top tech investors told him the U.S. economy and Wall Street depended on it.

Nvidia said Monday (November 23, 2026) that it had reinstated Mr. Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.

articles.title: Chief Minister inaugurates care home for elderly men
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan inaugurated Pithrumandiram, a new four-storey residential facility for 250 elderly men at Gandhibhavan in Pathanapuram the other day. Constructed at a cost of ₹20 crore by Lulu Group chairman Yusuffali M.A., the 40,000-square-foot complex provides dignified care and shelter for senior citizens abandoned by their families.

Designed with comprehensive medical and living amenities, Pithrumandiram features dormitories, adjustable beds for bedridden residents, palliative care, a pharmacy, a laboratory, and accessible infrastructure including two stretcher lifts. It also houses a 150-seat dining hall, prayer rooms, a library, and a 450-seat air-conditioned auditorium.

Speaking at the event, Chief Minister expressed grave concern over the rising neglect of senior citizens in Kerala. He said that the State government is considering strict legislation proposing up to three years of imprisonment for children who abandon their parents after usurping their property.

Mr Yusuffali said that abandoned elders deserve compassionate care. Pithrumandiram follows Mathrubhavanam, a ₹18-crore facility for female residents that Mr Yusuffali built and handed over to Gandhibhavan in November 2022.

articles.title: 18 minors were sexually abused by Gem Granites owner Veeramani: SIT
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Second chargesheet filed, arrest warrant issued against Prakash
In a startling revelation, the Greater Chennai Police on Wednesday said that 18 minors were sexually abused by Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani over a period of time.
The probe by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) so far into 9 cases registered against the octogenarian businessman and his associates had revealed the identity of 18 victims, police sources said.

Veeramani, Shanthi and 8 others have been arrested and lodged in the Puzhal central prison. They were arrested in connection with 8 cases booked under the Protection of Children from Sexual offences (POCSO) Act and one case of abetment to suicide involving a minor in 2004.

While the first chargesheet was filed in the designated special court for POCSO Act cases on November 11, 2026, and copies handed to the accused persons in the prison a week later, the second chargesheet was laid against Veeramani, Shanthi and their car driver Lazar on Monday.

In a related development, the special court has issued an arrest warrant against K. Prakash who is wanted by the police in connection with the cases involving Veeramani and others. A ‘Blue Corner Notice’ was already been issued to locate the location and activities of the accused person who is wanted in the criminal case. Investigators were following up their request with the Ministry of External Affairs to cancel the passport of Prakash, the sources said.

“The arrest warrant is required to intensify the efforts through the court and diplomatic channels to apprehend the accused (Prakash) and bring him back to Chennai. Efforts are on to file chargesheets in all the 9 cases against Veeramani and others,” a police officer said.

Investigation so far had revealed that 18 minors were sexually abused by Veermani and the number of victims could be more going by inputs that were received from different sources, the officer who did not want to be quoted said.

articles.title: Inscriptions offer valuable insights into achievements of past generations, says expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prof. Ramesh Nayak was delivering a special lecture at a programme organised jointly by Kannada University and Archaeology Department

Inscriptions are an invaluable source of information on the achievements, beliefs and way of life of people in the past and they play a crucial role in establishing historical facts and chronology, professor in the Department of Studies in Ancient History and Archaeology at Kannada University, Hampi, Ramesh Nayak has said.

Delivering a special lecture on “The heritage of inscriptions” at the university in Hampi on the occasion of World Heritage Week 2026-27, he said that inscriptions reflect the overall achievements of human civilisation and preserve information for future generations.
The programme was organised jointly by Kannada University and the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage, Kamalapura.

“Human beings have always been curious about the mysteries of nature. They have sought to pass on their experiences, knowledge and achievements to the coming generations. Since it is not possible to remember everything, people initially began recording information on material such as tree bark and animal skin. This practice gradually evolved into the tradition of engraving records on inscriptions,” Mr. Nayak said.
India’s vast store of knowledge is preserved in inscriptions, many of which provide important evidence for reconstructing the country’s history, he said.

“References to verses and other details in inscriptions help researchers understand the culture, administrative systems and historical developments of different regions. They also provide reliable evidence to establish chronology and study the social, religious, economic and political conditions of the period,” he said.

Presiding over the programme, Kannada University Vice-Chancellor D.V. Paramashivamurthy said: “The Halmidi inscription has long been regarded as the earliest Kannada inscription. However, subsequent research brought to light inscriptions such as those associated with Nandisena Muni, Tammatakallu and Talagunda are believed to predate it. The extent of Kannada used in these inscriptions continue to be a subject of scholarly discussion.”
Prof. Paramashivamurthy said that there is no conclusive evidence about the earliest language used by human beings.

“Several questions remain unanswered about the scripts used before the Ashokan inscriptions, as well as the nature of language and writing systems among tribal communities. These subjects require further research,” he said.

As historical evidence is gradually being lost, finding answers to such questions has become increasingly difficult and, therefore, discussions on the history of language and scripts have to be based on the available archaeological and historical evidence, he added.

Prof. Ramesh Nayak was delivering a special lecture at a programme organised jointly by Kannada University and Archaeology Department

Inscriptions are an invaluable source of information on the achievements, beliefs and way of life of people in the past and they play a crucial role in establishing historical facts and chronology, professor in the Department of Studies in Ancient History and Archaeology at Kannada University, Hampi, Ramesh Nayak has said.

Delivering a special lecture on “The heritage of inscriptions” at the university in Hampi on the occasion of World Heritage Week 2026-27, he said that inscriptions reflect the overall achievements of human civilisation and preserve information for future generations.

The programme was organised jointly by Kannada University and the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage, Kamalapura.

“Human beings have always been curious about the mysteries of nature. They have sought to pass on their experiences, knowledge and achievements to the coming generations. Since it is not possible to remember everything, people initially began recording information on material such as tree bark and animal skin. This practice gradually evolved into the tradition of engraving records on inscriptions,” Mr. Nayak said.

India’s vast store of knowledge is preserved in inscriptions, many of which provide important evidence for reconstructing the country’s history, he said.

“References to verses and other details in inscriptions help researchers understand the culture, administrative systems and historical developments of different regions. They also provide reliable evidence to establish chronology and study the social, religious, economic and political conditions of the period,” he said.

Presiding over the programme, Kannada University Vice-Chancellor D.V. Paramashivamurthy said: “The Halmidi inscription has long been regarded as the earliest Kannada inscription. However, subsequent research brought to light inscriptions such as those associated with Nandisena Muni, Tammatakallu and Talagunda are believed to predate it. The extent of Kannada used in these inscriptions continue to be a subject of scholarly discussion.”

Prof. Paramashivamurthy said that there is no conclusive evidence about the earliest language used by human beings.

“Several questions remain unanswered about the scripts used before the Ashokan inscriptions, as well as the nature of language and writing systems among tribal communities. These subjects require further research,” he said.

As historical evidence is gradually being lost, finding answers to such questions has become increasingly difficult and, therefore, discussions on the history of language and scripts have to be based on the available archaeological and historical evidence, he added.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: a timeline of events
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Over the last year, the traditional practice of lighting the Karthigai lamp at the Thiruppurankundram hill has faced uncertainty amidst petitions questioning where the lamp should be lit. Here is a timeline tracing key developments in the issue.

Detentions and protests marked this year’s Karthigai festival on November 24, 2026 in Thirupparankundram, the sacred hill known for its tradition of lighting the Karthigai lamp in Tamil Nadu every year. The police detained several senior leaders of the BJP, including State president Nainar Nagenthran. Protesters at the foothills were also detained.
The crux of these tensions is the ongoing issue of where the lamp is to be lit.

As the Karthigai Dheepam was lit the traditional place near Uchipilayar temple at Thirupparankundram Hindu outfits staged protest condemning the act of government, on November 24, 2026. | Photo Credit: G. Moorthy

Over the last year, the Madras High Court and the Supreme Court have heard petitions for lighting the lamp at a pillar near a dargah at the summit of the Thirupparankundram hill. Usually, the lamp is lit at a lower point. It was the case this year, too, notwithstanding a Supreme Court order that ordered the lamp to be lit at the pillar near the dargah.

This year’s festival might be over, but the long-standing issue is far from resolved. Disagreements over the use of the hill by the Muslim and Hindu communities, its ownership and traditional practices have existed since 1915. Now, with the apex Court’s order being a temporary arrangement, legal closure is yet to come.
Here is a timeline showing key developments over the years.

articles.title: ‘MyTDP’ has a million members now
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Marking the milestone, TDP national working president Nara Lokesh says the worker is the strength and force behind the party, and every effort will be made to recognise those who work for it
The official app of the Telugu Desam Party, MyTDP, has crossed one million membership milestone.

TDP national working president and IT Minister Nara Lokesh, in a post on X, said, “The worker is the leader. The worker is the strength, the force of the Telugu Desam Party. It is a great pleasure that the number of our family members registered on the ‘MyTDP’ app, created as a digital bridge between the party and its workers, has reached 10 lakh.”

Mr. Lokesh further said that every effort a worker makes on the ground must be recognised and every worker’s opinion must be valued. “Those who work hard for the party must be given appropriate opportunities. It was with this goal in mind that we launched the MyTDP app. My heartfelt congratulations to the 10 lakh members of the Telugu Desam family who have been part of this journey,” he said.

TDP State president and Gajuwaka MLA Palla Srinivasa Rao also expressed his delight as the number of members on the app reached one million. He extended his heartfelt wishes to the party’s national president and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Mr Lokesh, the entire TDP family and all party leaders and workers.

He noted that the app was initiated by Mr. Lokesh with the objective of identifying every party worker who toil at the grassroots level, ensuring their service were duly recognised and were given a rightful place within the organisation.

“The party’s strength lies in its workers,” Mr. Srinivasa Rao said, and expressed hope that this app would serve as a vital platform for valuing the opinions of every individual worker and providing them with appropriate opportunities.

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance

High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
